findings.where: First screen, the hero ground behind the heading, margin notes, actions and portrait (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pale gradient that runs from blue to lavender. That violet hue appears nowhere in the house colours. It also contradicts the tile's own palette specimen ('A warm paper… Three colours, no accent'; texture 'None… a flat warm tone'). The paper header above and the paper page below both meet the gradient at a hard seam, so the first screen reads as a separate tinted panel dropped between two warm grounds.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges the first screen first. The founder asked for a warm paper ground with only the house blue and grey as ink, and this first screen shows a third, cooler hue the specimen says isn't there. Mark wants nothing that reads 'techy' or slick, and a blue-violet wash is the look of a SaaS landing page, not a legal journal.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Write to me' and 'Book a consultation'
findings.fault: Both get the same solid house-blue fill with square corners, so they read as two equal primary buttons. 'Write to me' is a static label that does nothing when clicked, and the actual address beside it is grey text with a faint underline. The strongest colour on the page marks a dead box, and the real contact route gets the weakest treatment in the row.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who clicks the blue 'Write to me' box and nothing happens. The founder, who asked for one direct, personal way to reach Mark and gets two blue buttons competing for it.

findings.where: Margin notes on the first screen (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024) and the section labels below (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The house blue does two opposite jobs. The palette names it the colour of links and the action, but it is also used on every static margin note and section label. On this page blue doesn't tell a visitor whether something can be clicked: the notes look like links to the talks and go nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks 'Melbourne, 2026 LLM Course on PPP Law' expecting the talk and gets nothing. Angélique, who needs a clear rule for when blue means 'link' when she adds content.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' button on the PDF row
findings.fault: This action is a blue-outlined capsule with a round end, while every other action on the page is a square-cornered solid blue rectangle. The page has two button shapes and two fill styles with no difference in meaning to explain them.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will publish the PDF lists and needs one action style to copy. Visitors notice the inconsistency less, but it makes the set look unfinished.

findings.where: First-screen portrait (the 'exhibit') and its copy in the motion specimen
findings.fault: A static photograph has a wide soft drop shadow, which suggests it floats above the page or can be clicked. On the lavender hero the shadow comes out as a faint violet haze rather than a crisp lift. The tile frames the photo as an exhibit, but the shadow says 'card', not 'mounted object'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads the raised photo as clickable and taps it. The founder, who wanted an exhibit shown as a real object, which the precedent (Drawing Matter) does with a frame and caption, not a floating glow.

findings.where: The email address in the hero action row and in the footer
findings.fault: The same address is styled two ways. In the hero it is grey serif text with a light grey underline; in the footer it is blue sans with a blue underline. The parts map shows that only the footer one is a link, so the hero's version looks half like a link and isn't one.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the hero address expecting their mail app to open. The parts map shows it is static, so nothing happens.
